business_model.body: Archies designs and retails greeting cards, gifts and stationery products through a network of company-owned and operated retail outlets across India, alongside its own e-commerce platform archiesonline.com and tie-ups with third-party e-retailers and quick-commerce platforms. The Company has also been reorienting its strategy toward online and alternate selling channels, particularly for its stationery products.

- e-commerce / online platform

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Greeting cards industry in India remains unorganized with fragmented regional players; the Company is the leader with more than 50% share of the organized sector.
- Technology substitutes (e-greetings, SMS, Facebook, WhatsApp) have pressured greeting card demand, though management believes the segment has potential to bounce back.
- Realty sector stress and the mushrooming of organized retailing across the country are cited as factors shaping store-location strategy, driving a push for deeper penetration.
- E-commerce is cited as a catalyst offering round-the-clock availability, wider customer reach, speed and international reach.
- Management expects the greeting cards business to "show positive signs in the coming years" despite continuing pressure during the year.
- The gift segment has consistently contributed more turnover than the greeting card and stationery segments, and the Company is continuously adding products to this segment.
- Recent improvement in the export business, with the Company starting to receive export orders again, is cited as a positive development for future revenue and profitability.
- Tariff measures introduced by the Trump administration significantly impacted international trade and export orders during the year, per the Chairman's message.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Archies continues its retail expansion through company-owned/managed stores across Indian malls and high streets, opening 2 new Archies stores and closing 22 during the year, leaving 54 company-owned and operated outlets as on 31 March 2026, with plans to open more stores selectively going forward. Parallel to physical retail, the Company is expanding digitally through its own revamped e-commerce platform archiesonline.com and via Archies Global and Archies Online, plus tie-ups with third-party e-retailers (Flipkart, Snapdeal, Shopclues, etc.) and quick-commerce platforms.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- scale: leader of India's organized social-expressions industry — evidence: "the Company, which pioneered the concept in the Indian market, is the leader with more than 50% share of the organized sector"
- distribution: Pan-India retail footprint with company-owned/operated stores plus multi-channel e-commerce and quick-commerce tie-ups — evidence: "54 company owned and operated retail outlets" and tie-ups with Flipkart, Snapdeal, Shopclues and others; quick-commerce delivery "within 10 Minutes" — against it: the Company "opened total 02 retail stores and closed total 22 retail stores" during the year

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Social Expressions Industry in India is still unorganized, with numerous small regional players and very few nationwide players, creating persistent competitive pressure on Archies' organized-sector position.
- E-greeting, SMS and apps like Facebook and WhatsApp have taken a toll on greeting card business growth in general.
- Adversely affects the turnover of the Company, given the business is based on sentiment-driven purchasing.
- Poses a probable risk to the Company's turnover and profitability in its largest revenue segment.
- Emerging as an area of concern for the Company's retail store economics.
- The realty sector continues to be under stress while organized retailing is mushrooming in different parts of the country, affecting site selection and penetration strategy.
- A downturn in the economy, exchange rate fluctuation and natural calamities are likely to affect the business industry at large, per MD&A Risks and Concerns.
- Change in Government's fiscal policy has a bearing on the Company's performance, per MD&A Risks and Concerns.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Reorienting business strategy toward online platforms and alternate selling channels for Stationery Products, while continuing to consolidate Pan-India retail footprint.
- Expanding presence in e-commerce and digital space through Archies Global and Archies Online to reach a wider customer base.
- Continued focus on new markets and business initiatives, including exploring overseas markets.
- Sales optimization by creating a value proposition for the consumer, focused on customer satisfaction and value creation for profitability and sustainability.
- Continuing to open company-owned/managed stores in upcoming shopping malls and high streets on a selective basis.
- Tie-ups with quick-commerce platforms for rapid product delivery.

hero.oneLiner: Archies Ltd is the pioneer and leader of India's organized social-expressions industry, with more than 50% share of the organized greeting cards, gifts and stationery retail sector.
